data: This course examines the biological basis of behaviour and develops an understanding of the complexities of the brain and the mechanisms underlying various behavioural phenomena. How is our brain organised? How do neurons function? What is the brain's basis of psychological phenomena? How do our genes and hormones influence behaviour? We will be exploring answers to these questions through interactive lectures. This course introduces brain disorders as a clinical method to better comprehend the complexity of the mind-brain connection. In addition, we will discuss various techniques such as brain imaging and recording and how they unravel the mysteries of the brain. By integrating knowledge from biology and psychology, students gain a holistic understanding of how biological processes shape human behaviour and cognition. This course is designed to provide an introduction to the major concepts, theories, and methods in the field of behavioural neuroscience.
